metadata.title: PIRLS 2016 User Guide for the International Database: Supplement 1 International Version of the PIRLS 2016 Context Questionnaires
metadata.venue: IEA TIMSS & PIRLS International Study Center

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This document is a user guide supplement that provides the international version of PIRLS 2016 context questionnaires and the associated variable names. It does not describe an analytic sample, sampling frame, or any estimation procedure for student achievement outcomes, so survey weights and replicate-weight methods are not specified here. For analyses using the PIRLS 2016 international database, analysts should apply the complex survey design information provided in the main PIRLS technical documentation (e.g., student sampling weights and replicate weights) when producing population-representative estimates and standard errors. Because this supplement focuses on questionnaire content and derived-variable documentation references (Supplement 3), it should be treated as a measurement/data dictionary rather than an empirical results report.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values (PVs) are not applicable because this supplement does not analyze cognitive achievement outcomes or provide any PV-based scoring or modeling results. Instead, it documents questionnaire items and international variable names for PIRLS 2016 context questionnaires (student, ePIRLS, home, teacher, school, and curriculum). Missing-data handling is not reported because no dataset is analyzed and no imputation/deletion strategy is described.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: No analytic sample is defined in this supplement. It provides the international version of PIRLS 2016 context questionnaires and variable naming conventions; therefore, no inclusion/exclusion criteria for an analytic dataset are specified.

data.outcome_summary: This supplement is not an empirical study; it is a PIRLS 2016 user guide supplement that documents the international version of the PIRLS 2016 context questionnaires. It lists questionnaire sections (Student, ePIRLS, Home/Learning to Read, Teacher, School, and Curriculum) and provides item/question numbers, international variable names, and question text, including notes about which items are “trend” versus modified. The guide explains that countries may adapt certain wording or response options via national adaptations documented elsewhere (Supplement 2), while retaining the same basic interpretation. It also references derived variables used in PIRLS 2016 international results reporting (Supplement 3), but does not provide any achievement scaling, PV generation, or model-based results. As a result, there are no benchmarks, effect sizes, or predictive performance metrics reported in this document.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This record is a questionnaire documentation supplement rather than a research article. Consequently, fields that normally require empirical evidence—such as total sample size, country-level analytic Ns, PV handling, missing-data handling, and ML techniques—are not populated because the document does not conduct analyses or report results. The extraction is therefore limited to assessment instrument metadata (variable naming and questionnaire structure) and does not support inference about model performance or educational effects.
